packs.title: Towers, Stone and Sea
packs.promise: Read castle rooflines, a street tower and bay-area shapes beyond Nakanoshima.

q.s: Collect three different marks on one broad surface.
st: Find the broad Takoishi surface from an open stopped viewpoint, or use the photograph labelled F in the park’s highlights PDF.
Collect three visible differences: a lighter patch, a darker mark and an edge or join beside the large stone. Describe what you can actually see; no measurement is needed.
Rank your three discoveries by how much they stand out. Save the order and one reason without touching or tracing the masonry.

q.s: Make a tiny gallery from a building’s shapes.
st: Look at the museum’s central gable and window grid from a comfortable exterior viewpoint, or use the operator’s front-façade photograph.
Draw three separate thumbnail panels: one roof shape, one repeated window rhythm and one patch of shadow. Give each a short title of your own.
Arrange your panels into a tiny gallery and write why you chose that order. A written three-panel description is equally valid.

q.s: Collect three contrasts from an aquarium’s outside.
st: View the exterior from a stopped public space, or use the photograph in the operator’s Harbor Village page.
Collect three contrasts: a red area beside glass, a curved sea-creature form beside a straight edge, and a dark patch beside a light one. Temporary forecourt installations are optional.
Save your collection and choose which contrast would be easiest to recognize in a tiny drawing.

packs.title: Between Water and Stone
packs.promise: Find a quieter Osaka in bridge details, garden shapes and a few words beside the river.

q.s: Find a curve, a rhythm and a frame beside the water.
st: Choose a roomy stopping place at the bridge approach, clear of the crossing, station entrances and passing pedestrians.
Find a curve, a repeated shape and a frame in the bridge’s stonework, railing openings or lamps. An arch is one option, but a smaller curved detail counts too.
Imagine removing one of your three details. Describe what the view would lose: softness, rhythm, a boundary or something else.
Save the three details and the one you would keep first.

q.s: Collect living shapes without picking a thing.
st: Choose an open garden path and stop where you leave space for others. Stay outside planted beds.
Find three different shapes among a leaf, a stem, a bud or flower, and the edges of a planting bed. Flowers are optional.
Arrange the shapes in your note from simplest to most intricate. Explain one choice using a visible detail.
Save your small collection without picking or handling anything.

q.s: Give a park detail a brief imagined adventure.
st: Choose a comfortable public place near the lawn, clear of people walking, resting or playing.
Collect three visible ingredients: a path shape, a patch of shade and a colour from the city or planting around you.
Write a three-sentence imagined scene about a small object using those ingredients. The object can stay entirely in your story.
Save the scene and list the three details you borrowed.
